title: Neural Interpreter Mirror function codes
hypothesis: A one-angle Givens code on a shared sine/cosine interpreter matches a two-value unconstrained function code on held-out tasks and code composition while reducing actual serialized code-bank bytes.
physical_object: one shared phase-basis interpreter with four frequency signatures
mirror_coordinate: one phase angle per logical function; frequency is a shared-executor signature index
logical_multiplicity: many phase-shifted functions executed by one interpreter
controls: ordinary two-coefficient function code on same shared basis
fixture: f(x;s,phi)=sin(omega_s*x+phi), omega_s in {1,2,3,4}; adapt codes from 32 support points and evaluate held-out x; compose same-signature phase pairs

development.selection_metric: mean query NRMSE2 across phase-adapted logical functions and composed pairs

fresh.run_only_if: not applicable; deterministic code adaptation/algebra screen

storage.format: torch.save signature ids and adapted Mirror angles or coefficient vectors

compute.proxy: report 720-angle support search per function separately from two-coefficient least squares; report query basis and code decode MAC proxies

success_gate: Both worlds: Mirror and ordinary-code mean query NRMSE2 differ by <=1e-4; composition NRMSE2 <=1e-5 for both; Mirror serialized code payload is smaller.
failure_gate: Any development algebra, quality, or actual-byte gate misses.
boundaries: Analytic Fourier interpreter, not a learned Neural Interpreter.
Only phase-shifted functions are represented; signature family is fixed.
No language or broad task-composition claim.
